champion: Squamous cell carcinoma of the foot
ordered_diagnoses: Squamous cell carcinoma of the foot

facts.raw_span: A 60‐year‐old tailor with no significant medical history
a 3‐year history of macerated skin between his toes
a painful, fissured ulcer at the base of the fourth interdigital space of the right foot
which had been progressively enlarging over the past 18 months
received multiple antifungal regimens—including topical sertaconazole for 6 weeks and oral terbinafine 250 mg daily for 6 weeks—without improvement
a verrucous, infected ulceration with infiltrated, hyperkeratotic edges and a whitish, fissured base measuring 3 cm in diameter, extending onto the dorsum of the foot
Dermoscopy revealed unstructured whitish areas and hyperkeratosis
Popliteal and inguinal lymph nodes were not palpable
the remainder of the examination was unremarkable

rationales.F01: Patient's age and lack of medical history do not specifically point to any of the listed conditions.
rationales.F02: Macerated skin between the toes is a common symptom of interdigital conditions.
rationales.F03: The presence of a painful, fissured ulcer is highly suggestive of a chronic interdigital ulcer or hyperkeratotic foot ulcer.
rationales.F05: The lack of improvement with antifungal regimens suggests that the condition may not be fungal in nature.
rationales.F06: The description of the ulceration is consistent with a chronic interdigital ulcer, hyperkeratotic foot ulcer, or squamous cell carcinoma of the foot.
rationales.F07: The dermoscopy findings are consistent with a hyperkeratotic or chronic interdigital condition.
